title: AI Agent Threat Matrix 1.2
description: Shape of matrix.json. Technique ids are T-NNNN, or T-NNNN.NNN for a sub-technique; sub-techniques sit flat in techniques[] and carry parentId. The nine technique fields required by 1.1 are unchanged and still required. Every field added in 1.2 is optional. Added after the 1.2 release and required: wildPrevalence and wildSampleCount on every technique, and the top-level wildPrevalenceSource that says where and when they were read. scripts/validate_matrix.py checks this schema with an in-repo subset checker and then the cross-field rules the schema cannot express (see the x-semantic notes).

stixNamespace.description: UUID namespace for the deterministic STIX 2.1 ids in stix/agent-threat-matrix-bundle.json (uuid5 over this namespace and a canonical object name). Pinned: changing it changes every STIX id ever published.

dataSources.description: Registry of data sources a technique may cite in its dataSources array. May be empty.

mappingRelationship.description: SKOS mapping relation between the matrix technique and the external technique.

tactic.x-semantic: must be the id of an entry in tactics[]

attackClass.x-semantic: must be the id of an entry in attackClasses[]

dvaaValidation.description: Null when the technique carries no lab scenario.
dvaaValidation.x-semantic: must be null when evidenceTier is adapted

wildPrevalence.description: The wildPrevalence the registry endpoint in wildPrevalenceSource served for this technique on the read date, and 0 where it served none. The registry computes it from its honeypot telemetry as callbacks per page visit in the technique's category: callbacks divided by page visits, as a percentage rounded to two decimals and capped at 100, and 0 where the category has no page visits. The callbacks are the canary fires in the technique's category and the payload callbacks of the payloads mapped to the technique. It measures engagement with a honeypot, not a production attack rate. Written by scripts/sync_wild_prevalence.py, not by hand. Read it with wildSampleCount and the read date. It does not set or change evidenceTier.

wildSampleCount.description: The wildSampleCount the same endpoint served with wildPrevalence, and 0 where it served none: the callbacks plus the page visits behind that wildPrevalence, a whole number. 0 means the technique has no wild samples behind it.
wildSampleCount.x-semantic: must be above 0 wherever wildPrevalence is above 0

parentId.x-semantic: required if and only if id is dotted; must be the id of a technique in techniques[] and equal the part of id before the dot

dataSources.x-semantic: every value must be the id of an entry in the top-level dataSources[] registry

evidence.x-semantic: every entry must resolve to a source scripts/validate_matrix.py reads, and no entry may repeat another's type, reference and date: a honeypot-telemetry entry resolves when its reference is the wildPrevalenceSource url, its date is the wildPrevalenceSource read date and the technique's wildSampleCount is above 0; no other reference resolves

replacedBy.x-semantic: required if and only if status is deprecated; must be the id of a technique in techniques[]

version.description: Semantic version of this technique entry. Absent means 1.0.0.

id.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique or sub-technique id
MITRE ATLAS technique or sub-technique id

type.description: Kind of publicly resolvable source the reference points at.

wildPrevalenceSource.description: Where and when the wildPrevalence and wildSampleCount of every technique were read. scripts/sync_wild_prevalence.py writes it with them.

url.description: The registry endpoint the values were read from.

read.description: The date the endpoint was read.
